about.title: La Quinta Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: La Quinta residents rely on countless manufactured products every day — from vehicles crossing Washington Street and Highway 111 to household tools, recreational gear, and appliances used across the city's neighborhoods and resort communities. When one of those products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing defect, or a missing warning, the resulting injury can be sudden and serious. California's strict liability framework means an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That distinction matters, because it can shift focus away from lengthy negligence arguments and toward the product itself. Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers along Riverside County's supply chains can share responsibility. If a defective product injured you or someone in your family in La Quinta, LawProactive offers a free, no-obligation way to connect with an independent attorney who works on contingency and can evaluate what happened.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. Under California's strict liability rules, you generally only need to show the product had a defect — in design, manufacturing, or warning — and that the defect caused your injury. This is different from many other injury claims that require proving fault.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including packaging, instructions, and any broken pieces. Don't attempt repairs or discard it, since the product itself is often central evidence in a defect claim.
